correctness.rationale: The identity XY=r(X)×c(Y) makes every product an idempotent rectangle and characterizes the idempotent rectangular band. All automorphisms must permute the square fibers and act by independent bijections of row and column supports. Inclusion–exclusion gives exact fiber sizes \(F_{u,v}\); singleton fibers distinguish cardinality-one supports, and strictly increasing minima \(F_{u,2}=3^u-2\) recover every row-support size (and symmetrically column sizes) for both base dimensions at least two. Conversely all size-preserving support permutations and all fiber bijections fixing the rectangle are automorphisms; consistent fiber labeling splits the extension. The semidirect product, orbit count and degeneracy case follow. The separate \(2\times2\) multiplication checks exhaust the 2880 proposed mappings; small finite calculations are corroboration, not a proof of all dimensions. No scientific claims beyond the proven finite semigroup result are made.

value.rationale: The 2026 survey explicitly motivates full power-semigroup automorphism groups, and the exact behavior can be dramatically nonrigid outside cancellative settings. Here a natural complete infinite two-parameter family is solved, including all automorphisms (not merely those induced from the underlying band), their exact order and orbit partition. The support-fiber sizes count finite bipartite graphs without isolates; their strict profile determines the unexpectedly large symmetric-kernel factors. Already the \(2\times2\) base has 2880 power automorphisms versus four band automorphisms. The complete structural classification answers a mathematically motivated invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice or raw finite census.
